en.sup: Supplied in English. The Hebrew has no verb: 'persons to the LORD'.

03.r: The descendants of Israel, the whole people.
03.n: Literally 'sons of'; STEP tags it here as 'people of', and the BSB folds the phrase into 'the Israelites'.

04.r: The people named after Jacob, whose second name was Israel.
04.n: BDB: the second name of Jacob, and the name of the Hebrew nation.

05.r: Moses is to pass the law on.
05.n: A perfect with 'and' after a command, which continues the command: literally 'and you shall say'. The Douay-Rheims and YLT keep that form.

07.n: The Hebrew puts 'a man' first: 'a man, when he vows'. STEP tags it here with the general sense 'anyone', and the BSB says 'someone'.

08.r: Introduces the case the law covers.

09.r: A vow out of the ordinary, set apart from the usual offerings.
09.n: Gesenius gives the root's proper sense as TO SEPARATE, TO DISTINGUISH; BDB gives 'be surpassing, extraordinary'. So 'make a special vow', a vow set apart. The translations differ widely: 'singular', 'clearly utter', 'accomplish', 'wonderful'.

10.r: A promise to give something to God.
10.n: Gesenius gives two senses, a vow and anything vowed, such as a vowed sacrifice.

11.r: At the price fixed for each person in the verses that follow.
11.n: The brief's lexicon gives estimate, valuation; Gesenius's first senses are a row or pile and a putting in order, and BDB says it is made by ordering, classifying. 'Your' addresses Moses, or whoever sets the value; the same 'your valuation' recurs through the chapter, and it may have become a fixed term for the standard rate. That last point is a reasonable reading, not a lexicon statement.

12.r: Human beings vowed to God, whose value is then paid instead.
12.n: The plural of the word often rendered 'soul'. BDB lists this verse under its sense 'persons'. The Douay-Rheims's 'his soul' takes the vow as of oneself.

13.r: The persons vowed belong to God.
13.n: The 'to' here marks belonging: they are the LORD's, as YLT puts it.

07.n: ὃς ἄν, 'whoever': the Greek folds 'a man, when' into one phrase.

09.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. 'Whoever vows a vow': the Greek has nothing for 'special'.

11.n: ὥστε τιμήν, 'so as to pay the price': τιμή, 'price, value', is the Greek word for the valuation.

12.n: Our Greek text reads only 'the (...) of him' here; a noun, probably 'soul', has evidently dropped out after the article. That is an inference from the gap.
